blocks.content: The Gupta Empire is known as the 'Golden Age of Ancient India'. It witnessed great achievements in administration, science, literature, art, and culture.
1. Rise of the Gupta Empire

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Gupta Empire was founded by Sri Gupta, but Chandragupta I raised its status by adopting the title Maharajadhiraja.
Samudragupta expanded the empire through military campaigns and was hailed as the 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith.
Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) extended the empire to the western coast by defeating the Shakas and patronized the Navaratnas (Nine Gems).
The Gupta period is known as the 'Golden Age of India' due to major advancements in art, science, mathematics (Aryabhata), and Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa).
Huna invasions and weak local administration contributed to the eventual decline of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century.

blocks.content: • The Gupta Empire was founded by Sri Gupta around 240 CE.
• The Guptas initially ruled a small kingdom in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
• The real expansion of the empire started with Chandragupta I.
• Chandragupta I assumed the title 'Maharajadhiraja'.
• His marriage with Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi strengthened the Gupta power.
2. Important Gupta Rulers
3. Samudragupta (335–375 CE)
• One of the greatest rulers of the Gupta dynasty.
• Known as the 'Napoleon of India' because of his military conquests.
• Information about his conquests is found in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription.
• The inscription was written by Harisena, his court poet.
• He performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice.
4. Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) (380–415 CE)
• He expanded the Gupta Empire further.
• He defeated the Shakas and gained control over western India.
• His court was famous for the 'Nine Gems (Navaratnas)'.
• The famous Chinese traveler Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.
5. Administration of the Gupta Empire
6. Economy of the Gupta Period
• Agriculture was the main occupation.
• Land revenue was the main source of income.
• Trade and commerce flourished during this period.
• Gold coins known as 'Dinaras' were issued by Gupta rulers.

rows: Prayag Prashasti inscription by Harisena; performer of Ashvamedha sacrifice; issued gold coins playing the Veena.
Defeated Shaka Kshatrapas; hosted the Nine Gems (Navaratnas) including Kalidasa; visit of Faxian.

blocks.content: 7. Art and Architecture
• Gupta art is considered the classical phase of Indian art.
• Ajanta caves contain beautiful paintings of the Gupta period.
• Temple architecture developed significantly.
• Example: Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh.
8. Literature and Education
9. Science and Technology
• Aryabhata discovered that the Earth rotates on its axis.
• The concept of zero was developed.
• Advancements were made in astronomy and mathematics.
10. Decline of the Gupta Empire
• Weak successors after Skandagupta.

items: Harisena composed the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) in Sanskrit, detailing the military conquests of Samudragupta.
Chinese traveller Faxian (Fa-Hien) visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II to collect Buddhist scriptures.
Nalanda University was established during the reign of Kumaragupta I.
Aryabhata wrote Aryabhatiya and Surya Siddhanta during the Gupta period, introducing the concept of zero and calculating the value of Pi.

blocks.content: • Hun invasions weakened the empire.
• Economic problems and administrative weaknesses.
SSC Exam Important Facts
• The Gupta period is known as the Golden Age of Ancient India.
• Samudragupta is called the Napoleon of India.
• Fa-Hien visited India during Chandragupta II's reign.
• Gold coins of the Guptas were called Dinaras.
• Aryabhata was a famous scientist of the Gupta period.
